h1: Nevada Convention Hotel Ubon Ratchathani — a convention hotel with an in-house water park near the airport
intro: If you're looking for a place in Ubon where the kids can splash around all day without ever leaving the grounds, or you need to host a seminar or Chinese banquet and want your guests staying in the same building — Nevada Convention Hotel is a name Ubon locals have known for years · It's a large 3-star convention hotel with 150 rooms on Chayangkun Road, near Ubon Ratchathani airport · What sets it apart from other hotels in town is the in-house Nevada Water Park in the same grounds, with both indoor and outdoor pools, plus large meeting and banquet halls · It opened back in 2003 and had a major renovation in 2019 · The rooms are spacious, parking is free, and prices start at around THB 650/night · On TripAdvisor it scores about 3.4 out of 5 (16 reviews), ranked #14 of 28 hotels in Ubon

body.html: Who Nevada Convention Hotel is for — if you had to sum up its character in one line, Nevada Convention Hotel is "Ubon's veteran convention hotel with a water park built in" · It's not a small boutique hotel selling style, and it's not a brand-new luxury property where every corner is flawless · It's a large 150-room hotel designed from the start to handle conferences, banquets, tour groups, and big families · It opened back in 2003 and went through a major renovation in 2019, so some parts look fresher while others still carry the feel of an older building · From reading the actual reviews, the people who suit it best are families bringing kids to play at Nevada Water Park, organizers of seminars and Chinese banquets who want guests staying in one building, tour groups, and self-driving travelers who need easy parking · The ones who may not click with this style are couples after a newer design or a quiet, romantic atmosphere, and anyone expecting room standards on par with an international chain · Put simply, if you value "plenty of space, everything in one place, and an easy-to-reach price" over "newness and luxury in every detail," Nevada makes sense · And to be straight from the start: the review scores here are fairly split — there are plenty who are very happy and plenty who came away disappointed, which we'll cover honestly in the sections below

Location and getting around — Nevada Convention Hotel sits at 434 Chayangkun Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, a main road on the north side of town that connects to the city center and runs out toward the airport · The clearest advantage of this location is that it's very close to Ubon Ratchathani airport (UBP) — just about 3-4 kilometers, or roughly 10 minutes by car, which is great if you've just flown in and want to reach your room quickly, or have an early flight to catch · The hotel offers an airport shuttle too, so let them know in advance when you book · It's also near several key spots, such as a university and a sports stadium within a few hundred meters, and it's about 6 kilometers from Ubon Ratchathani train station · Getting to the city center around Thung Si Mueang and the Ratchabut night market isn't far either, around 10-15 minutes by car or ride-hail · Chayangkun is a big road with malls, gas stations, and restaurants spread along its length, so finding food near the hotel is no trouble · The honest caveat: because it's right on a main road, rooms facing the street can catch some traffic noise at times, and the hotel isn't in a walkable downtown area, so without your own car you may need Grab or a taxi to head into town · But for self-drivers, this location is easy to get in and out of, with plenty of parking

"Brought the kids to play in the hotel's water park all day without driving anywhere — they loved it. The rooms are spacious, the staff are helpful, there's lots of parking, and it's close to the airport. Great for a family trip."

Room types and decor — being a large 150-room hotel, Nevada offers several room types to match your group size and budget · The main types you'll see on booking platforms are the Deluxe Room (king or twin beds, spacious, with a window), pool-view / pool-side rooms (Pool Side / Pool View) that look out over the pool and fountains, which some reviewers say have the nicest atmosphere, and Suites for those who want more space or are traveling as a family · The point reviewers agree on is that the rooms are spacious with large bathrooms — an upside of an older building laid out with bigger rooms than newer towers that pack in more units · In-room amenities cover the basics: air conditioning, fridge, work desk, TV, blackout curtains, and some rooms have a balcony or terrace · But to be straightforward, this is where the reviews split most clearly into two camps · The satisfied side says the rooms are clean, spacious, and worth the price · The disappointed side talks about rooms that look dated for the building's age, furniture and fittings starting to wear in places, fairly firm beds, and a musty smell or dust in overlooked corners of some rooms · Some older reviews even mention insects in the room, so it's worth checking the room's condition at check-in and asking to switch immediately if you find any · The bottom line on rooms: space is the strength, but newness and upkeep details are things you should set your expectations around, in line with the price and the hotel's age

Facilities, pools, and the water park — this is genuinely Nevada's main selling point · The hotel has both indoor and outdoor swimming pools, and what makes it more special than the average hotel is the in-house Nevada Water Park in the same grounds, with water-play attractions, a kids' pool, and a family splash area · This is what families bring up most often, because you can let the kids play in the water all day without traveling anywhere · Beyond the pools and water park, it has the full set of big-hotel facilities: spa, restaurant, cafe, bar, karaoke, convenience store, playground, and large meeting and banquet halls that can host seminars, weddings, and Chinese banquets for several hundred people — which is why the word Convention is in the name · There's an airport shuttle, luggage storage, laundry, taxi booking, Wi-Fi, and free parking that's roomy, which self-drivers praise often · One thing that comes up in reviews is that the outdoor pool gets fairly strong sun with not much shade, so midday in the hot season can be intense — better to swim in the morning or evening · And as with the rooms, some common areas show their age, but in terms of "everything in one place," Nevada does well at this price point

Food and dining — the hotel has an in-house restaurant, cafe, and bar, plus karaoke rooms, which fits its character as a place geared toward banquets and groups · On breakfast, it has to be said straight that the information differs from one platform to another — some sources say breakfast is included on certain rates, while others say there's no breakfast service · So the thing to do is check clearly when you book whether your chosen rate includes breakfast, and if breakfast matters to you, ask the hotel directly to confirm · On taste and quality, reviews are fairly middle-of-the-road — some say there's a decent selection, others feel it's still ordinary · The upside of the location is that Chayangkun Road has restaurants and convenience stores all along it, and the hotel has its own convenience store, so finding food is no trouble · For main meals, many people choose to drive or take a Grab into downtown Ubon, where there are more good places to eat · Overall, food at Nevada isn't the reason to come for in-hotel dining — it's a convenient extra for when there's an event or you don't feel like going out

Service — service is the area where Nevada earns fairly consistent praise in the actual reviews, even though the hotel's overall score is split · The words that come up often are "friendly staff" and "helpful", and foreign reviews use exactly those — friendly and helpful · Many say the team takes good care of guests, especially when you come as a group or have a conference, which is what the hotel does best · There are reviews praising the meeting rooms as well organized and good value, well suited to seminars · That said, to be straightforward, a few voices in the reviews note that the care can be uneven at certain times — for example, sometimes it's hard to find staff at the counter late at night, or responses are slow at some points, which is common in large hotels juggling several things at once · Overall, service is a strength that helps prop up the stay, especially for groups and families

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling together from Trip.com, Agoda, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly clear that this is a hotel where opinion splits into two camps more than most, so we'll tell both sides honestly · On the praise side: spacious rooms and large bathrooms, a water park and pools where kids can play all day in one place, friendly and helpful staff, a location near the airport with easy access to town, roomy free parking, meeting rooms that handle events well and good value, and an easy-to-reach price that's worth what you get · On the caveats side: the thing mentioned most is the building and rooms looking dated for their age — some liken parts of it to "having been built a long time ago," even with the 2019 renovation · Next come fairly firm beds, air conditioning that doesn't get fully cold or has dust in some rooms in the hot season, Wi-Fi that's unstable in spots, and little shade at the outdoor pool, with some older reviews mentioning a musty smell and insects in the room, which is more about specific rooms than the hotel as a whole · The numbers reflect this: on TripAdvisor around 3.4 out of 5 from 16 reviews, ranked #14 of 28 hotels in Ubon, which is middle-of-the-road · The takeaway: people who understand they're staying at a veteran hotel focused on space and activities tend to be happy, while those expecting newness and polish tend to be disappointed — setting your expectations right is the single most important thing

"The pool and water park are great — the kids played all day. But the room itself looked a bit dated and the bed was firm. Next time, if we're coming to swim it's fine, but if we're just staying over, I'd pick somewhere newer."

Price and value — Nevada's room rates start at around THB 650/night for a basic room at normal-season prices, and climb from there depending on room type, season, and festival periods, with suites or high season rising into the low to mid thousands · Compared with Ubon hotels in a similar price range, Nevada's clear advantage is that it has a water park and pools for the kids, large meeting halls, and spacious rooms, at a lower price than newer hotels · If you're coming as a family who wants the kids to swim, or as a group that needs to run a conference or Chinese banquet, the value here is in "getting everything in one place" without paying a premium · But if you're traveling solo or as a couple to explore the city, and you value newness, quiet, and room design, you may find that in-town hotels like Sunee Grand, Laithong, or a condo-style stay like Excella fit your needs better for similar money · To be clear: Nevada is great value for groups and families who use the facilities fully, but it won't be the best value if you don't use the pools, water park, or meeting rooms at all

Good to know before you book — here's a rundown of what to check before you hit book, so the stay goes smoothly and there are no surprises · One: check whether your room rate includes breakfast, because the information differs across platforms — ask the hotel to confirm if breakfast matters to you · Two: if you're coming to swim, check the opening hours of the water park and pools and ask whether water park entry is included with your room, since the water park may have a separate rate at certain times · Three: if you want the nicest atmosphere, try asking for a pool-view room or one not facing the main road to cut down traffic noise · Four: because it's an older building, it's worth asking for a recently renovated room or one in good condition and checking the room as soon as you check in — if you find a musty smell, dust, or any issue, ask to switch right away · Five: if you're coming as a group or hosting an event, contact the hotel's sales team directly — you'll usually get a better meeting-room-plus-room package rate than booking room by room · Six: if you're self-driving, parking is roomy and free with easy access — a perk you can make full use of

The verdict — Nevada Convention Hotel isn't a brand-new hotel and it isn't a stylish design stay, but it is a large veteran convention hotel with an in-house water park, spacious rooms, free parking, and a location near Ubon airport, at an easy-to-reach price · Its clear strengths are the water park and pools where families can let the kids play all day, large meeting halls for seminars and Chinese banquets, plenty of space, friendly service, and everything in one place · The honest trade-offs are the building and rooms looking dated for their age, fairly firm beds, uneven room upkeep in some rooms, and review scores that are fairly split · If you're a family who wants the kids to swim, a seminar or banquet organizer, a tour group, or someone self-driving who values space and a full set of facilities in one place — Nevada is an easy-to-understand, good-value choice · But if you're here to explore the city as a couple or solo and you value newer rooms, quiet, and design, take a look at options like Sunee Grand, Laithong, or Excella in town instead — they'll suit your style of stay better

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Nevada Convention Hotel Ubon Ratchathani

faq.q: Where is Nevada Convention Hotel in Ubon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The hotel is at 434 Chayangkun Road, Nai Mueang, Mueang Ubon Ratchathani, on a main road on the north side of town · Its standout point is that it's very close to Ubon Ratchathani airport (UBP), about 10 minutes by car (~3-4 km) · It's near a university and a sports stadium, about 6 km from the train station · Getting to the city center around Thung Si Mueang is about 10-15 minutes by car

faq.q: Does Nevada Convention Hotel really have a water park and swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes, it does · The hotel has both indoor and outdoor swimming pools, plus the in-house Nevada Water Park in the same grounds, with water-play attractions and a kids' pool · It's the main selling point that lets families bring kids to play in the water all day · The caveat is that the outdoor pool gets strong midday sun with not much shade, so morning or evening is better for swimming · You should check the opening hours and water park entry fee when you book

faq.q: What's the starting price at Nevada Convention Hotel, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 650/night for a Deluxe Room at normal-season rates · There are pool-view / pool-side rooms at around THB 850, family rooms at around THB 1,100, and suites at around THB 1,500 · Most rooms are spacious with large bathrooms · Prices shift with the season and festivals, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Nevada Convention Hotel best suited for?
faq.a: It suits families bringing kids to swim, organizers of seminars and Chinese banquets, tour groups, and self-drivers, because of the in-house water park, large meeting halls, spacious rooms, and free parking · It's less suited to couples or solo travelers after newer rooms, stylish design, and a quiet atmosphere — in-town hotels like Sunee Grand or Laithong would suit them better

faq.q: Does Nevada Convention Hotel have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: On breakfast, the information differs across platforms — some room rates say breakfast is included, while other sources say there isn't any · We recommend checking clearly when you book or asking the hotel to confirm · As for parking, it's free and roomy with easy access — a plus for self-drivers · There's free Wi-Fi, though it isn't stable everywhere

faq.q: What's Nevada Convention Hotel's review score, and is it dated?
faq.a: On TripAdvisor it scores around 3.4 out of 5 from 16 reviews, ranked #14 of 28 hotels in Ubon, which is middle-of-the-road, and opinion is fairly split · The hotel opened in 2003 and was renovated in 2019, so some parts still look dated for their age · The points that earn praise are the water park, spacious rooms, friendly service, and good value, while the criticisms are dated rooms, firm beds, and uneven room upkeep in some rooms
